mcqs.question: What is the correct definition of bond enthalpy?

options.A: Energy required to break one mole of a particular type of bond in gaseous molecules under standard conditions
options.B: Energy released when a mole of atoms forms a metallic lattice
options.C: Energy change accompanying a phase transition of a substance
options.D: Energy needed to remove an electron from a gaseous atom

mcqs.answer: Energy required to break one mole of a particular type of bond in gaseous molecules under standard conditions
mcqs.explanation: Bond enthalpy (also called bond dissociation energy) is the amount of energy required to break one mole of a specific type of bond in the gas phase, measured under standard conditions. Options B, C and D describe lattice enthalpy, enthalpy of phase change, and ionisation energy respectively, which are different concepts.

mcqs.question: Among the following diatomic molecules, which has the highest bond order?
mcqs.explanation: Bond order is the number of shared electron pairs between two atoms. N₂ has a triple bond (bond order = 3), O₂ a double bond (2), and F₂ and Cl₂ single bonds (1). Hence N₂ possesses the highest bond order.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate bond order to length and strength
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between bond order, bond length and bond strength?

options.A: A higher bond order corresponds to a shorter bond length and greater bond strength
options.B: A higher bond order corresponds to a longer bond length and weaker bond strength
options.C: Bond order does not affect bond length but only influences bond strength
options.D: Bond order only determines the bond angle in a molecule

mcqs.answer: A higher bond order corresponds to a shorter bond length and greater bond strength
mcqs.explanation: Increasing bond order means more shared electron pairs, pulling the nuclei closer (shorter length) and creating a stronger bond. Options B, C and D contradict the established trend.

mcqs.question: In a spectroscopic measurement the distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms in a molecule is found to be 1.54 Å. What term best describes this measured distance?
mcqs.explanation: Bond length is the distance between the nuclei of two atoms joined by a chemical bond. Bond angle refers to the angle between two bonds, bond enthalpy to the energy required to break a bond, and bond order to the number of shared electron pairs.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines a bond angle?

options.A: It is the measure of the angle between two adjacent bonds in a molecule
options.B: It is the distance between two bonded atoms
options.C: It is the energy required to break a chemical bond
options.D: It is the number of electron pairs shared between two atoms

mcqs.answer: It is the measure of the angle between two adjacent bonds in a molecule
mcqs.explanation: A bond angle is the geometric angle between two lines representing two bonds that have a common atom. Options B, C and D describe bond length, bond enthalpy and bond order respectively, which are common misconceptions.

mcqs.question: If breaking one mole of H–Cl bonds in the gas phase requires 431 kJ of energy, what is the bond enthalpy of the H–Cl bond?
mcqs.explanation: Bond enthalpy is the energy needed to break one mole of a specific bond under standard conditions; therefore the given 431 kJ directly equals the H–Cl bond enthalpy. The other numbers are unrelated fractions or zero, which are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Compare the bond orders of carbon monoxide (CO) and nitric oxide (NO). Which statement is correct?

options.A: CO has a higher bond order than NO
options.B: NO has a higher bond order than CO
options.C: Both CO and NO have the same bond order
options.D: Neither CO nor NO possesses a defined bond order

mcqs.answer: CO has a higher bond order than NO
mcqs.explanation: In molecular orbital theory, CO has a bond order of 3, whereas NO has a bond order of 2.5. Hence CO’s bond order is higher. Options B, C and D are therefore incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate bond order to length and strength
mcqs.question: The bond lengths of N≡N, O=O and F–F are approximately 1.10 Å, 1.21 Å and 1.42 Å respectively. Which of the following statements best reflects the relationship between bond order, bond length and bond strength?

options.A: As bond order increases, bond length decreases and bond strength increases
options.B: As bond order increases, bond length increases and bond strength decreases
options.C: Bond order has no systematic effect on bond length or strength
options.D: Higher bond order always leads to a larger bond angle

mcqs.answer: As bond order increases, bond length decreases and bond strength increases
mcqs.explanation: Higher bond order means more shared electron pairs, pulling atoms closer (shorter length) and creating a stronger bond, as seen in the decreasing lengths from F–F (single) to N≡N (triple). Options B, C and D contradict the established trend or refer to unrelated parameters.
